items.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then we’d drive to Brooklyn to get Jimmy Garrison.

ctx.x: Perhaps you hit on what is really fundamentally the key here, and that is that spiritual element.

That’s part of it. That’s not only it. It’s more than that. It’s something he knew. Something he knew. I know sometimes I’d be in Philly when he was playing out there. He’d just be around there – when I was with Bird, he’d just stay in the audience, not acting big or knowing too much. Listen. At one period he lived in Queens. I lived in Queens. He called me up. Or maybe – what was the guy used to be the road manager for Miles and him? I forget his name. He also lived in Queens. He called me probably first and…

dingling on the piano. We go and play some more. He would close his eyes, and before he was finished, the waiters were taking the chairs, putting them on the tables. Half the people had left. I’d walk down the stairs. I had a taxi waiting for me, holding my insides like this after playing, but feeling like I’ve done something. That’s – I never had that experience with anybody. You want to know about John Coltrane. Getting back to Chicago, it’s time to go home now, Sunday night. He’s staying upstairs somewhere,…
